# Arithmetic-buffer zero/positive parity separation and an actual zero-fiber descent

This note retains the positivity boundary of the arithmetic parameter problem. It proves an exact arithmetic status separation for deepest sources, without assuming regular caps or parameter differentiability. It then computes a genuine compatible shape descent at the previously exhibited full-concave arithmetic optimum with a whole zero fiber. Neither statement excludes all zeros at an arbitrary bad joint body minimum.

The fixed-body example being varied is `candidate ec7a5867f3acc4b0`. The ordinary depth-continuity and whole-own-fiber cap arguments used below are proved in `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96` and the buffered-depth continuation sources.

## 1. Actual arithmetic-buffer setup

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base, with positive compatible convex d-fibers K_p and canonical hull C. Put N=d+1, dm=sum_p dX|K_p, M=dm(S), and let E_p(y) be ordinary projective energy. Let L>=0 be a continuous concave parameter with arithmetic normalization

    integral_S L dm=M.

For a fixed positive definite continuous covector norm Gamma, set

    f(p,y)=[L(p,y)E_p(y)/M]^(1/N).

The buffered depth at w=(p,y) is the infimum of its unchanged pure-base cap masses and the masses of all nonvertical caps

    a.Z+u.X >= a.p+u.y-epsilon f(p,y)Gamma(u).

Let Q>0 be its maximum over sampled marks and I its deepest-base set. Assume every deepest mark is own-interior and its depth is strictly smaller than its atomic base depth. This hypothesis, including attainment of an own-proper active nonvertical cap, is automatic at sufficiently small positive epsilon in a fixed positive family, uniformly over ALL admissible L; Section 3 supplies the details.

The real full-space function F(z,y)=E_(C_z)(y)^(1/d) is jointly concave. Therefore f=M^(-1/N)L^(1/N)F^(d/N) is jointly concave. Its buffered upper level regions are convex. Directly, for any fixed nonvertical normal the allowed mark inequality is a linear functional minus epsilon times a concave function bounded by the right mass-Q quantile. Pure-base depth upper regions are also convex. This conclusion does not require a positive parameter at every deepest mark.

## 2. An attained proper cap forces equality in every sampled anchored relation

Choose deepest own-interior marks w_i=(p_i,y_i), positive weights lambda_i summing to one, and suppose

    q=sum_i lambda_i p_i belongs to P,
    w=sum_i lambda_i w_i.

Actual compatibility makes w own-interior at q: convexly combine an own ball from each positive input. Convexity of the buffered level region gives depth at least Q, and sampled maximality makes it exactly Q.

Take an attained own-proper mass-Q cap at w and normalize Gamma(u)=1. Write

    t=a.q+u.y-epsilon f(w),
    t_i=a.p_i+u.y_i-epsilon f(w_i).

Its mixed tail is continuous in the threshold. Its own proper section has positive coarea, so the tail strictly decreases immediately to the right of t. Since the tail at t is Q, the RIGHT mass-Q quantile is exactly t. Every endpoint is deepest, so its cap in this same normal has mass at least Q, and hence t_i<=t. Consequently

    t <= sum_i lambda_i t_i <= t.

The first inequality is precisely concavity of f. Thus every inequality is an equality and

    f(w)=sum_i lambda_i f(w_i).                       (1)

This argument handles arbitrary supporting statuses on the other fibers. It does not assume a globally strictly decreasing tail or identify left and right quantiles across a plateau: properness at the selected threshold is exactly what removes that local plateau.

Now suppose some positive input has L_i=0 and another has L_i>0. All F_i are positive because all marks are own-interior. Write B for the positive-L inputs. Weighted Holder gives

    sum_i lambda_i f(w_i)
      <=M^(-1/N)(sum_i lambda_i L_i)^(1/N)
                         (sum_(i in B)lambda_i F_i)^(d/N).

Joint concavity of L and F gives the same lower bound for f(w) with the last sum replaced by sum_ALL lambda_i F_i. This is STRICTLY larger, because omitted zero-L inputs have positive F_i. This contradicts (1).

**Status heredity.** No anchored convex representation of a sampled deepest mark can use both zero-L and positive-L deepest inputs.

For a midpoint the strictness has the explicit lower bound

    f((w_0+w_+)/2)
       >=(f(w_+)/2)(1+F(w_0)/F(w_+))^(d/N)
        >f(w_+)/2                                   (2)

when L(w_0)=0<L(w_+).

Let Z be the bases supporting a zero-L deepest mark, and J the bases supporting a positive-L deepest mark. A zero at an own-interior point forces a nonnegative concave function to vanish on that whole fiber. Therefore Z and J are disjoint and partition I. Relation (1) also proves separately

    conv(Z) intersect P=Z,   conv(J) intersect P=J.   (3)

For Z, any positive f at the formed sampled mark would violate (1); for J, concavity gives a strictly positive value at the formed mark. Finally a zero and a positive deepest base cannot have the same integer parity: their midpoint would be sampled by lattice completeness and would violate status heredity. Hence

    occupied_parities(Z) intersect occupied_parities(J)=empty,
    k(Z)+k(J)=k(I)<=k(P).                            (4)

These are exact arithmetic structural statements. They do not bound the exterior mass or give a Gamma payment for either class.

## 3. Why the proper-cap hypotheses hold uniformly for small epsilon

Arithmetic normalization and nonnegative concavity imply

    max_(K_p)L <= N M/|K_p|,
    E_p<=|K_p|,
    0<=f<=N^(1/N).                                  (5)

For a fixed positive family, the uniform strip bound therefore gives

    0<=D_epsilon(w)-D_0(w)<=C epsilon                (6)

at every sampled mark and every admissible parameter, with C depending only on the section-area bound and Gamma. Original depth vanishes at every own-fiber boundary point, by the finite-base supporting-plane extension. Its positive maximum Q_0 and continuity imply that every buffered maximizing mark has a fixed own inball when epsilon is sufficiently small.

The exact ordinary inequality

    D_0(p,y)<=baseDepth(p)-|K_p|/2

combined with (6) gives a strict atomic gap at each such mark, uniformly once C epsilon<min_p |K_p|/4. For rank-zero bases, use the formal baseDepth=M; the same inequality follows from opposite continuous caps.

To obtain an attained cap, normalize Gamma(u)=1. The own threshold u.y-epsilon f is bounded. For the finite other fiber thresholds, the fixed-base linear-programming clamp retains proper/supporting thresholds and replaces strict full/empty ones by thresholds outside the common support range. Its minimum-norm base coefficients have a uniform bound. A minimizing sequence thus has an actual nonvertical limit cap of mass Q. It cannot capture the entire own fiber: any ambient cap containing that whole fiber has mass at least baseDepth(p), by separating p from the convex hull of the bases not wholly captured. It contains the own-interior source, so its own trace has positive volume. Hence the own cut is proper, as required in Section 2.

The same proof is uniform on any fixed compact positive-body class with uniform section, volume, inball and covariance bounds. It invokes neither a SAME response separator nor a C1 cap-mass assumption.

## 4. Exact joint descent of the known whole-zero-fiber optimum

For a in [1/16,3/16], take the actual centered interval family

    P={-1,0,1},  (V_-,V_0,V_+)=(a,1,1),
    M=a+2,  Sigma=(a^3+2)/[12(a+2)].                 (7)

The interval roof is strictly compatible at the middle. Every proper closed-minor quota is strict: all singletons have mass less than M/2, and each consecutive pair has mass less than M. This remains true after small changes of a.

Over ALL nonnegative continuous concave arithmetic-normalized parameters, the unique sampled optimum for 0<epsilon<=10^(-4) is

    L_a(z,x)=(a+2)(1+z)/3.                           (8)

Here is the complete parameter and depth check. At Y=(0,0), a finite affine supporting majorant A=ell+b z+c x has b<=ell-a|c|/2<=ell from nonnegativity at the left endpoints. Its actual mixed average is ell+(1-a)b/M. Therefore 1<=3ell/M and L(Y)>=M/3. Equality forces b=ell,c=0 and L=A on the sampled fibers, giving (8).

For the parameter (8), E_0(y)=1-4y^2 and its middle-center displacement is

    delta_0=epsilon sqrt(Sigma/3).

The exact two-endpoint interval clipping formula gives endpoint capture infimum a at the center for this nonnegative displacement. The own interval contributes 1/2+delta_0. Steep finite base tilts attain that value. At any other middle mark, the same two steep orientations give the upper bound

    a+1/2-|y|+delta_0 sqrt(1-4y^2),

strictly smaller. The left endpoint maximum is a/2, because L vanishes there. The right endpoint has upper bound 1/2+epsilon sqrt(2Sigma/3), below the middle value throughout the stated range. Thus the unique global deepest mark is Y and

    Q_epsilon(a)=a+1/2+epsilon D(a),
    D(a)=sqrt[(a^3+2)/(36(a+2))],
    beta_epsilon(a)=Q_epsilon(a)/(a+2).              (9)

For any other admissible L, the lower bound on L(Y) makes its value at Y at least (9). Strict inequality in L(Y) strictly increases the own proper interval capture; (5) keeps every displacement in the proper range. This proves the full-class fixed-body optimum, rather than only an affine ansatz.

Now decrease a along a(t)=a-t and keep the other two interval fibers fixed. This is an ACTUAL nested convex-body path. In ambient coordinates it is defined by -1<=z<=1 and

    2|x|<=1,
    2|x|<=1+(1-a+t)z.

The changed roof shrinks just the sampled left fiber and leaves the two other sampled fibers exactly fixed. Reoptimize by (8), or equivalently restrict the old L_a and multiply it by M_t/M. The removed sampled mass was entirely at L_a=0, so this is exactly its arithmetic renormalization. Covariance is updated using (7).

Differentiating the exact global value, with no optimizer derivative assumed, gives

    beta_epsilon'(a)
      ={(3/2)[1+epsilon D(a)(a^2(a+2)/(a^3+2)-1)]}
                                                   /(a+2)^2.

Since a<=1, Sigma<=1/12 and D<=1/6. Hence

    beta_epsilon'(a)
      >=(3/2)(1-epsilon/6)/(a+2)^2>0.               (10)

Therefore the actual path t>0 has strictly negative normalized derivative. In particular the original a=1/8 arithmetic optimum with its entire zero endpoint fiber is not a joint body minimum. The calculation retains original mass, covariance, energy and arithmetic renormalization, rather than importing logarithmic amplification.

This is a genuine exclusion of the precisely described centered three-interval stratum. It does not exclude a zero fiber at a different joint minimum, a zero facet inside a positive fiber, or an arithmetic optimum under a different normalization.

## 5. What still prevents a general zero-cut conclusion

If an actual body cut removes mass r_0 on which the old parameter is exactly zero, arithmetic renormalization is L_new=(M_new/M)L on the retained body. Consequently

    L_new E_new/M_new=L E_new/M

exactly: mass renormalization cancels in this product. This is useful when a source fiber is unchanged, but the CURRENT covariance norm still changes. It cannot be omitted or replaced by an L-weighted covariance without changing the objective.

For a cut near a zero facet rather than on a whole zero fiber, the removed integral of L is positive and the cancellation is only approximate. The gain is of order removed mass, with no logarithmic factor. A general exclusion would need to control the actual cap losses, energy changes, covariance change and the positive/zero parity split together. Sections 2 and 4 provide rigorous pieces of that problem, not its closure.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_arithmetic_zero_parity_and_interval_descent_slab_recovery.py` checks the exact normalization, parameter bound, covariance and derivative identities and the interval range margins. The general parity statement is proved analytically in Sections 1--3.

# Arithmetic-buffer zero/positive parity separation and an actual zero-fiber descent

**Arithmetic buffer status separation at deepest sources**

In the source's buffered auxiliary model, take epsilon>0, a finite lattice-complete family of positive fibers, a nonnegative continuous concave arithmetic profile L with integral L dmu=M, and a fixed positive definite continuous covector norm Gamma. Assume the stated positive compact-family/strict atomic-gap conditions and attainment of the deepest sources by proper own caps. For f=(L E/M)^(1/(d+1)), any sampled convex combination anchored at a deepest source satisfies the source's equality relation for f. In particular a deepest source with L=0 and E>0 cannot mix with a deepest source with L>0; the two statuses occupy disjoint parity classes. This conclusion is about deepest-source status in that buffered model, not all source mass or an exclusion of zero-L deepest sources.

Scope limits: Convex-hull/status closure concerns deepest bases, not all sampled mass. The note also contains a separate explicit interval descent; no general exclusion of zero fibers follows.
